title: The Compaction Cliff in Long-Running AI Agent Memory

visual_explainer.question: Why does uniform compaction erase safety-critical state, and where can type-aware retention intervene?
visual_explainer.takeaway: Knowledge Triage classifies retained items once, then applies type-specific compaction, decomposition, retrieval, and a guard verifier instead of treating every token as equally lossy.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Type-blind compactors and score-only retrieval under shared artifact budgets, with downstream token matching only partial.

analysis.tldr: Uniform compaction can erase safety constraints far faster than other agent state. Under shared output budgets, TypeCompact preserves constraint recall of 1.00/0.95/0.80 at 50/25/10% compression versus best type-blind results of 0.53/0.39/0.24. The guarantee is conditional on classifier recall, typed retrieval receives metadata unavailable to score-only controls, and downstream retail gains are not token-matched.
analysis.problem: A safety rule and an episodic log compete for the same context budget even though the rule may require exact preservation while the log can tolerate summarization.
analysis.core_idea: Classify working-set items into types once, then route them through fidelity-specific compaction, constraint-replicating decomposition, scoped retrieval that pins applicable constraints, and post-operation verification.
analysis.agent_loop: classify retained item → compact/decompose/retrieve by type → verify classified constraints → accept next working set or escalate unsafe
analysis.retrieval_design: TypeRetrieve adds stored type, topic, and query-topic scope metadata to a fixed dense substrate, then pins all in-scope constraints before relevance-ranked residual items. This is a richer interface package, not a score-only ranking comparison.
analysis.evidence: Budget-matched compaction preserves constraints 2–4x better across ratios and 0.96 after five rounds. TypeDecompose removes locality violations at 14.5% mean token overhead. TypeRetrieve reaches 1.00 recall@50 versus 0.91 for dense retrieval, but uses privileged typed scope metadata.
analysis.why_it_matters: It makes retained-state value conditional on semantic type and turns compaction, partitioning, retrieval, and verification into one explicit policy surface.
limitations: The guarantee preserves only constraints the classifier flags; corpus recall is about 0.87 and SafetyMargin about 0.93.
Classifier/materialization cost is excluded from zero-token operator tables.
Typed retrieval uses author-tagged topics and a 50-query, 33-policy-chunk setup, so interface observability is unmatched.
Retail downstream comparisons retain 1,136 versus 669 tokens; a token-matched behavioral control is missing.
Type-aware retention deliberately sacrifices belief and preference fidelity, and public-GitHub type distributions may not transfer.
